 Europe News Polish gunman who killed 6 people in Krakow has 'ultranationalistic' views, minister says
 Published Sat, Nov 7 2026 11:33 AM EST Updated Sat, Nov 7 2026 5:39 PM EST WATCH LIVE Emergency responders gather after a deadly shooting on Nov. 7, 2026 in the Main Market Square of Krakow, Poland. At least five were killed and more were injured in the incident, according to initial reports in Polish media. Omar Marques | Getty Images News | Getty Images A Polish man with far-right views drove into a busy central square in Krakow on Saturday and opened fire, killing six people and injuring 15 others before police shot and wounded him, authorities said.
 The attack, which Poland's defense minister described as an "act of terror," happened in Main Square, which is in the heart of Krakow's Old Town and is a major tourist hub in the country's second-largest city.
 The 25-year-old attacker drove to multiple spots in the square and opened fire at each stop with an automatic weapon, authorities said. Although they didn't release his name, Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the man holds "very radical" and "ultranationalistic" views.
 "Everything indicates that he was fascinated by far-right ideologies," Kierwiński said at a news conference.
 Hours after the attack, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said authorities found the bodies of three of the suspect's close family members — two women and a man — inside his home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, a city about 150 kilometers (93 miles) northeast of Krakow.
 "We have the next acts of this tragedy," Tusk told reporters.
 Four women and two men were killed in the Krakow attack. At least three of the women were Polish, and one of the dead was a U.K. citizen, authorities said at a news conference. Police were still trying to identify the other two people who were killed.
 Authorities said a total of 13 people were hospitalized in serious condition, though that figure may include the gunman, who underwent surgery after the attack.
 It's unclear how many of the injured were shot. Two of them were treated and released within hours of the mass shooting. Two police officers were among the injured, including one whose injuries were serious, Kierwiński said. Also injured in the attack were five non-Poles, police commander Marek Boroń said.
 People were wounded at several locations
 The attacker wore military-style fatigues and a bulletproof vest, and used a military-type long gun, Krakow police spokesperson Katarzyna Cisło said. Police found many other weapons and ammunition in his car. He kept firing at the police even after being shot himself, she said.
 The attacker engaged in a "wild ride" around Main Square, which is why people were wounded at several locations, Cisło said.
 Cisło added that the gunman acted alone and that the public is safe.
 Krakow mayor Łukasz Gibała said the city will be in official mourning until Wednesday. He vowed that Krakow will remain open to visitors despite the tragedy.
 "The square will belong to us again," Gibała said in a video posted to X.
 Mass shootings are rare in Poland
 Videos posted on social media by witnesses show people running away from the square to take cover on small streets nearby, as well as first responders trying to resuscitate victims. In one video, a police officer is seen repeatedly shooting the attacker, who is lying on the street, only to later slowly collapse to the ground.
 Photos showed a Polish Medical Air Rescue helicopter after it landed in the square.
 Emergency responders gather after a deadly shooting on Nov. 7, 2026, in the Main Market Square of Krakow, Poland. At least five were killed and more were injured in the incident, according to initial reports in Polish media. Omar Marques | Getty Images News | Getty Images It was not immediately clear whether the firearm used in Saturday's attack, or the guns found in the perpetrator's car, were legal. Around 411,000 people hold gun permits in Poland, which has a population of 37 million, and interest in gun ownership has been rising.
 Mass shootings are uncommon in Poland. However, in mid-October, three attacks at schools in the central province of Mazovia took place within four days, leaving one person dead and many wounded, including children.
 In a post on X, Tusk praised the police officers who responded to Saturday's tragedy. President Karol Nawrocki said his thoughts were with the victims, the wounded and their families.
 A tram driver reported around 3 p.m. that his vehicle was shot at by a man in a moving car while passing nearby the main square, the Krakow municipal transport company said. The tram driver's cabin window was shattered.
 Animal rights group OTOZ Animals said the attacker also shot two horses. Both animals are alive, but one was grazed by a bullet and the other hit in the leg. White carriages drawn by horses are a main tourist attraction in the square.
 Warsaw mayor Rafał Trzaskowski announced increased security measures, including road barriers, along main streets in the old town in the Polish capital after the Krakow attack.
